turns.content:
Okay — let’s build a master checklist for our cross-country move from Ohio to Oregon (me, my partner, and our dog). I want it broken into phases (3+ months out, 2 months, 1 month, 2 weeks, 1 week, moving day, post-move), with clear tasks, who’s responsible (me, partner, or joint), estimated time required for big items, and priorities. Include:

- housing tasks (ending lease/selling, utilities, change of address)
- vehicles (driving vs shipping, registration/inspection issues)
- movers vs DIY (quotes, insurance, deposits)
- packing timeline and room-by-room packing checklist + declutter tips
- important paperwork to gather and keep with us
- finances and budget line items (deposits, travel, pet fees, temporary housing)
- dog-specific checklist (vet records, travel comfort, overnight arrangements)
- timeline for cancelling/starting services and subscriptions
- suggested 6–8 week calendar of reminders we can sync with our phones
- a printable one-page “moving day essentials” checklist to keep with the car

We’re aiming to move in about 10 weeks. Budget currently flexible but we want ballpark costs for DIY vs movers and vehicle shipping. Start with the full phased checklist and then give a compact printable one-page moving-day essentials.

# Ohio → Oregon Move: Master Checklist

**Assumptions:** Move is ~10 weeks out. Responsibility defaults are **M** (me), **P** (partner), or **J** (joint). Swap them as you like. Cost figures are 2024–2025 ballparks; get live quotes. Verify DMV rules at the official Oregon DMV and Ohio BMV sites before you act, since requirements change.

---

## PHASE 1: Weeks 10–9 (Catch-up on "3+ months" items)

**Housing**
- [ ] **J** Check lease end date and notice requirement (often 30–60 days). Send written notice. *(Priority: HIGH, 30 min)*
- [ ] **J** If you own: list the home or line up a sale timeline. Book a realtor interview. *(HIGH, 2–4 hrs for research)*
- [ ] **M** Research Oregon neighborhoods, rentals, and commute. Set a search budget. *(MED, 2–3 hrs)*
- [ ] **P** Check whether your employer offers relocation assistance or remote work arrangements. *(MED, 1 hr)*

**Movers vs. DIY**
- [ ] **J** Get 3–4 binding/non-binding estimates from licensed interstate movers. Verify USDOT numbers on FMCSA's SAFER site. Ask for in-home or video estimates. *(HIGH, 3–5 hrs total)*
- [ ] **J** Price a DIY truck (U-Haul, Penske, Budget) and a portable container (PODS, U-Pack). *(HIGH, 1–2 hrs)*
- [ ] **M** Decide: full-service, hybrid (movers for the big stuff, you drive the car), or DIY. See the cost table below.

**Vehicles**
- [ ] **J** Decide: drive, ship, or fly-and-rent. Get 2–3 vehicle shipping quotes if shipping. *(HIGH, 1–2 hrs)*
- [ ] **M** Schedule a pre-move maintenance check: oil, tires, brakes, battery, fluids. Oregon's mountain passes and heat both matter. *(MED, 1 wk lead time)*

**Pet**
- [ ] **M** Book a vet visit for a health check and a copy of all records (rabies certificate, vaccines, microchip number, medications). *(HIGH)*

---

## PHASE 2: Weeks 8–7 (~2 months out)

**Housing**
- [ ] **J** Sign a rental or confirm a closing date in Oregon. Get a lease copy or closing docs and save them to a "Move" folder. *(HIGH, 2–4 hrs)*
- [ ] **J** Book temporary housing for the first 1–2 weeks if your new place isn't ready (dog-friendly Airbnb or extended-stay). *(MED, 1 hr)*
- [ ] **M** Start a utilities map: which providers serve the Oregon address, and their setup lead times. Electric and gas often need 3–7 days' notice; internet installs can take 2+ weeks. *(MED, 1–2 hrs)*
- [ ] **J** Schedule internet installation in Oregon now. It's the most backlogged item. *(HIGH)*

**Movers / Booking**
- [ ] **J** Select your mover or truck. Book the date. Read the contract for **valuation coverage**. Released value is about 60¢/lb per item and nearly worthless; Full Value Protection is worth paying for. *(HIGH, 1–2 hrs reading)*
- [ ] **J** Pay deposits only after verifying the company's USDOT number, reviews, and insurance certificate. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** If DIY: reserve the truck or container for the pickup date. *(HIGH)*

**Vehicle**
- [ ] **M** If shipping: book the carrier and choose open (cheaper) or enclosed (~$500+ more). Confirm pickup window and whether the carrier needs keys or a driver contact. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** If driving: plan a route with dog-friendly stops and lodging. Book 2–3 nights ahead on high-demand dates. *(MED, 2–3 hrs)*

**Pet**
- [ ] **M** Confirm the dog can travel by car. Test a 20–30 min drive and note any anxiety or motion sickness. Discuss medication with the vet if needed. *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Get a Health Certificate (CVI) only if flying or if your vet recommends it. Ask your vet. *(LOW–MED)*

**Documents**
- [ ] **J** Gather paperwork (see Documents section). Put originals in one folder you carry in the car.

**Finances**
- [ ] **J** Build the budget. Open a separate "Move" savings or spending account if helpful.

---

## PHASE 3: Weeks 6–4 (~1 month out)

**Housing**
- [ ] **J** Send formal notice to current landlord or list your house. Request a move-out inspection and deposit return address. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Schedule utility shutoffs and final reads in Ohio for the day after you leave. Keep your end date flexible. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** Confirm the Oregon utility start dates in writing. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Start your change-of-address at USPS (usps.com) about 2 weeks before the move, so it activates on time. *(HIGH)*

**Vehicle**
- [ ] **M** Check your Ohio title and registration. You'll need the title to register in Oregon. If there's a loan, contact the lienholder about title or payoff.
- [ ] **M** Check emissions and inspection rules. Oregon requires a DEQ emissions test if you register in the Portland metro area (Clackamas, Multnomah, Washington counties) or Medford/Klamath Falls areas. Find out where you'll register first. *(MED, 1–2 hrs research)*
- [ ] **M** Begin Oregon DMV plan: new residents typically have a short window (verify, often ~30 days) to get an Oregon license and register vehicles. Gather documents now. *(HIGH)*

**Pet**
- [ ] **M** Update the dog's microchip registry to the new address after you arrive, or set a reminder. Note the Oregon dog license requirement (county or city). *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Find a new vet near Oregon. Ask for records transfer. *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Book the first Oregon vet visit for a few days after arrival, and identify emergency vets along your route and at destination. *(MED)*

**Packing**
- [ ] **J** Start declutter (see Packing section). Start with garage, storage, closets. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Order boxes, tape, bubble wrap, markers. Ask about free boxes from liquor stores and grocery stores. *(MED)*

**Employment and Admin**
- [ ] **P** Tell your employer your move date. Ask about remote-work policy, relocation reimbursement, and paperwork. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Check if you need to notify Ohio tax authorities of a part-year resident status. Keep records of your move date. *(MED)*

---

## PHASE 4: Weeks 3–2 (2 weeks out)

**Packing**
- [ ] **J** Begin packing non-essential rooms (guest room, storage, decor). See the room-by-room list.
- [ ] **J** Pack a "Last Out, First In" box for each room.
- [ ] **J** Sell, donate, or give away items you won't move. Schedule pickups. *(HIGH)*

**Movers / DIY**
- [ ] **J** Confirm the mover's arrival window, crew size, and payment method. Get the final written estimate. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** If DIY: confirm truck or container pickup and drop-off times. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Ask about a Tuesday or Wednesday delivery if you need flexibility. *(LOW)*

**Vehicle**
- [ ] **M** If shipping: confirm pickup date, location, and carrier contact. Remove personal items (car shipping insurance doesn't cover them). *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** Finish maintenance. Check registration and insurance card. *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Buy or get an insurance policy that covers you in Oregon. Call your current insurer. Ask about out-of-state coverage and moving the policy. *(HIGH)*

**Pet**
- [ ] **M** Order a dog ID tag with your new phone number or get a temporary tag that includes your destination address. *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Set up a pet-sitter or boarding option for moving day if the dog would be stressed by packing. *(MED)*

**Services**
- [ ] **J** Schedule final services in Ohio (cable, water, trash). Schedule Oregon starts for the arrival date. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Notify banks, credit cards, insurers, and the Social Security Administration of your address change (see Services section). *(HIGH)*

**Finances**
- [ ] **J** Check your budget. Pay down or set aside money for deposits (first month, last month, security deposit) and a 2-week contingency fund.

---

## PHASE 5: Week 1 (1 week out)

**Packing**
- [ ] **J** Pack everything except daily essentials and the moving day kit.
- [ ] **J** Defrost and clean the fridge and freezer 24 hrs before the move (if the mover requires it or you're driving a truck). Donate perishable food.
- [ ] **J** Take photos of valuables and serial numbers. Keep them on your phone and a USB drive. *(HIGH)*

**Movers / DIY**
- [ ] **J** Confirm the mover's appointment, arrival time, and payment. Give a copy of the inventory. Confirm access (elevator, parking, permits). *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** If DIY: load a practice run and confirm your truck or container is reserved. *(MED)*

**Pet**
- [ ] **M** Confirm overnight plans on each lodging night for the dog. Pack food, water, bowls, leash, poop bags, meds, vet records, blanket, favorite toy, and calming aids. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** Give the dog a vet check if any symptoms arise and confirm the Oregon vet appointment.

**Services**
- [ ] **M** Confirm the Ohio utility shutoffs and Oregon starts. Confirm internet install.

**Vehicle**
- [ ] **M** If driving: service the car if needed, fill tank, check tires, and pack the emergency kit (see one-pager).

---

## MOVING DAY

- [ ] **J** Take a final walk-through photo or video of each room, closets, and the outside.
- [ ] **J** Read the Bill of Lading before signing. Note any damage on the inventory. Don't sign blank forms.
- [ ] **J** Keep the Bill of Lading and inventory with your documents.
- [ ] **J** Return keys, garage remotes, and fobs to the landlord or realtor. Get a receipt.
- [ ] **J** Do a final meter read and photograph it.
- [ ] **M** Keep the dog in a crate or secure room away from movers. Give the dog a familiar bed and toy.
- [ ] **M** Start the trip early, in the morning if possible. Plan breaks every 2–3 hours for the dog. Keep the car cool and don't leave the dog alone in a parked car.
- [ ] **P** Keep a log of mileage, fuel, and lodging for tax and reimbursement records.

---

## POST-MOVE: First 2 Weeks

**Housing**
- [ ] **J** Photograph the new place at move-in. Note any damage and send it to the landlord in writing within the deadline. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Confirm utilities are on and working. Test internet. Locate the water shutoff, breaker box, and gas shutoff. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Get renter's insurance active on the day you take keys. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Change locks or confirm the previous tenant's codes have been changed. *(MED)*

**Vehicles and DMV**
- [ ] **M** Get an Oregon driver's license (bring proof of residency). Check whether you need to pass a test. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** Register your vehicle with Oregon DMV. Bring the title, proof of insurance, odometer statement, and VIN verification if required. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** If the vehicle needs an emissions test, schedule it. *(HIGH if Portland metro)*
- [ ] **M** Cancel Ohio registration and plates after Oregon registration is complete.
- [ ] **M** Update insurance to Oregon address. *(HIGH)*

**Voting and Civic**
- [ ] **J** Update voter registration. Oregon automatically registers eligible DMV customers; confirm your status at sos.oregon.gov. *(MED)*

**Dog**
- [ ] **M** Get the first Oregon vet visit done. Transfer records. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** Update microchip registry with new address. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** Get the Oregon dog license from your county or city. *(HIGH, usually required)*
- [ ] **M** Find the nearest 24-hour emergency vet and save the number. *(HIGH)*

**Finances and Tax**
- [ ] **J** File part-year resident returns for Ohio and Oregon when tax season comes. Keep your move-date records. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Update your address with banks, cards, and employer payroll. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Keep moving receipts for potential deductions or reimbursement. *(MED)*

**Services**
- [ ] **J** Confirm all cancellations in Ohio are finished (see services list). *(MED)*

---

## DOCUMENTS TO GATHER AND KEEP WITH YOU

Keep these in a single folder or pouch in the car, not in a moving truck.

- [ ] Driver's licenses (both of you) and passports if you have them
- [ ] Vehicle titles, registrations, and insurance cards
- [ ] Lease or closing papers for both homes
- [ ] Moving contract, estimate, Bill of Lading, and inventory
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt and carrier contact
- [ ] Dog: rabies certificate, vaccine records, microchip number, medication list, vet contact, recent exam notes
- [ ] Medical records and prescriptions (copy of each person's current prescriptions)
- [ ] Birth certificates, marriage certificate, Social Security cards (or copies)
- [ ] Passports for dependents, if applicable
- [ ] Bank and credit card account contact numbers
- [ ] Employer offer letter or relocation agreement
- [ ] Tax records from the last 2–3 years (store digitally too)
- [ ] School or childcare records, if applicable (none listed here)
- [ ] Insurance policy numbers (home or renters, auto, health)

---

## FINANCES AND BUDGET

Estimates are for a 1–2 bedroom household plus one dog, Ohio to Oregon (~2,400–2,500 miles). Get real quotes.

| Fuel for truck | $700–$1,000 | n/a | ~8–10 mpg |
| Full-service movers (2 bedrooms) | n/a | $5,000–$10,000+ | Packing and loading included |

# Part 1: Room-by-Room Packing Checklist

**Box estimates** assume a 2-bedroom home. For a 1-bedroom, cut each room's count by about 30–40%. Times are for one person packing carefully. Two people working together typically finish in about 60% of the listed time.

| Room | Boxes (2BR) | Pack time | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Garage / storage** | 4–8 | 4–8 hrs | **J** (start first) | Drain and dispose of fuel, propane, paint, aerosols, and chemicals. Movers won't carry hazmat. |
| **Kitchen** | 12–15 | 6–8 hrs | **J** | Pack last-used items last. Keep a "first night" box for coffee, plates, pet food, and a pan. |
| **Living room** | 4–6 | 2–3 hrs | **J** | Electronics go in original boxes if you have them. Photograph cable setups. |
| **Primary bedroom** | 6–8 | 3–4 hrs | **M** or **P** | Pack off-season clothes first. Keep out a week's worth of outfits. |
| **Second bedroom / office** | 5–8 | 3–4 hrs | **M** | Files and cables take longer. Label cables with tape and a color code. |
| **Dining room** | 2–4 | 1–2 hrs | **P** | Wrap china individually. Use dish packs for stacks. |
| **Bathrooms** | 2–3 | 1 hr | **P** | Leave out toiletries, meds, and towels until the final day. |
| **Linen / hall closets** | 2–3 | 1 hr | **P** | Keep one set of sheets and towels separate. |
| **Dog area** | 1 | 30 min | **M** | Keep food, bowls, leash, meds, records, and toys in the car, not in a truck. |
| **Basement / attic** | 4–10 | 4–6 hrs | **J** | Often the biggest source of unwanted items. |

**Box quantities:** Expect roughly 40–60 boxes for a 2BR and 25–40 for a 1BR. Get about 10% more than you think, since you'll need extras for fragile and odd-shaped items. Common sizes: small (books, weigh under 40 lb), medium (kitchen and clothes), large (bedding and light items only).

## Declutter Tips

- **Weight is money.** Movers price by weight, and a 2BR with heavy books and tools can add hundreds of dollars. Sell or donate heavy, low-value items first.
- **Use a 3-pile method.** Keep, sell, donate. Anything you haven't used in 12 months and wouldn't buy again goes to sell or donate.
- **Start with the hard zones.** Garage, storage, and basement take the longest. Start there in week 8 and week 7.
- **Sell fast, donate fast.** List large items on Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist 3–4 weeks out. Schedule charity pickups for week 2–3.
- **Don't move:** half-used cleaning products, expired food, damaged furniture, pressure-treated lumber scraps, and anything with a battery or fuel.
- **Consider local or cheaper replacements.** Mattresses, cheap furniture, and small appliances are often cheaper to replace in Oregon than to move.

## Labeling System

1. **Color-code by room.** Use a colored tape or dot for each room. Example: blue = bedroom, green = kitchen, yellow = living room, red = fragile, orange = garage.
2. **Number each box with a room code.** Use an ID like K-01, K-02, BR1-03. Write the same number on the top and two sides.
3. **Write three things on each box:** room code, a short contents summary ("Kitchen – pots & pans"), and a priority tag: **OPEN FIRST**, **FRAGILE**, or **LOAD LAST**.
4. **Keep a box log.** Use a Google Sheet or phone notes with columns for Box #, Room, Contents, Priority, and Value (for high-value items). Take a photo of each high-value box's open contents.
5. **Tell the movers.** Give them the log so they know what's where, and mark "Do not load" boxes that ride in your car.

---

# Part 2: Calendar Reminders (8 Weeks)

Dates are relative to **Move Day (M)**. Start at **M−56** if you're beginning now and have 8 weeks. If your move is 10 weeks out, the first two weeks overlap with the earlier phases, so start there.

## How to Sync

- **Google Calendar (easiest):** Paste the events into a Google Sheet with your move date in cell B1. Use a formula like `=$B$1-56` for each event's date, then import the CSV into Google Calendar. Choose a dedicated "Move" calendar so you can hide or delete it all at once.
- **Apple Calendar:** Import the Google calendar to your iPhone (add the Google account in Settings > Calendar), or make a new calendar in Apple Calendar and add events manually.
- **Shared:** Both partners should subscribe to the same calendar. Use the **Assignee** tag in the event title.

## Event List

Format: **Title** | Date | Duration | Owner | Notes

**Week 8 (M−56 to M−50)**
- **Declutter kickoff: garage & storage** | M−56 | 2 hr | J | Start the sell/donate piles.
- **Book car maintenance** | M−55 | 30 min | M | Oil, tires, brakes, battery. Book a slot for week 5 or 6.
- **Lease notice / listing check** | M−54 | 1 hr | J | Confirm notice was sent. If you own, check the listing timeline.
- **Dog vet visit + records** | M−52 | 1 hr | M | Ask for a copy of all records and a health certificate if needed.
- **Dog car ride test** | M−50 | 30 min | M | Practice with the crate or harness. Note anxiety or motion issues.

**Week 7 (M−49 to M−43)**
- **Order packing supplies** | M−49 | 30 min | J | Boxes, tape, bubble wrap, markers.
- **Verify and book movers or truck** | M−47 | 1 hr | J | Confirm USDOT number, insurance, and Full Value Protection before paying.
- **Book dog-friendly lodging** | M−45 | 1 hr | M | Book 2–3 nights if driving. Confirm pet fees.
- **Schedule Oregon internet install** | M−44 | 30 min | J | This is the most backlogged item, so confirm the date.
- **List large items for sale** | M−43 | 2 hr | J | Furniture, bikes, tools, extra appliances.

**Week 6 (M−42 to M−36)**
- **Tell employer your move date** | M−42 | 30 min | P | Ask about remote work, relocation, and payroll address changes.
- **Check Ohio title, lien, and Oregon emissions rules** | M−40 | 1 hr | M | Find out whether you need a DEQ test in your registration county.
- **Declutter pass 2: closets & kitchen** | M−38 | 3 hr | J | Donate what you haven't used this year.
- **Confirm lease notice deadline met** | M−36 | 15 min | J | Notice periods are often 30–60 days.

**Week 5 (M−35 to M−29)**
- **Sign Oregon lease / confirm closing** | M−33 | 1 hr | J | Save copies to your Move folder.
- **Get renter's insurance quote** | M−31 | 45 min | J | Start coverage on the day you get keys.
- **Set up Oregon utilities** | M−30 | 1 hr | J | Confirm start dates in writing.
- **Schedule donation pickup** | M−29 | 30 min | J | Book a pickup or drop-off date.

**Week 4 (M−28 to M−22)**
- **Start packing: guest room & decor** | M−28 | 3 hr | M/P | Pack items you won't need until arrival.
- **Schedule Ohio shutoffs + final reads** | M−25 | 30 min | J | Set the day after you leave. Keep the end date flexible.
- **Refill prescriptions** | M−23 | 30 min | M | Ask for 30–90 days so you're covered during the move.
- **Pack storage / rarely used rooms** | M−22 | 4 hr | J | Basement, attic, and extra closets.

**Week 3 (M−21 to M−15)**
- **Notify banks, cards, insurers, SSA** | M−21 | 1 hr | J | Update addresses. Note the change date.
- **Order dog ID tag** | M−18 | 15 min | M | Include a temporary contact number.
- **Confirm mover arrival window** | M−16 | 30 min | J | Ask for the crew size and payment method.
- **Pack the rest of the house, except essentials** | M−15 | 4 hr | J | Keep out a "first week" set.

**Week 2 (M−14 to M−8)**
- **Submit USPS change of address** | M−14 | 20 min | J | Set the activation date to move day or the day after.
- **Donation / sell pickups** | M−13 | 1 hr | J | Clear the house of items you're not moving.
- **Vehicle service visit** | M−12 | 2 hr | M | Recheck tires and fluids if you're driving.
- **Confirm car shipping pickup** | M−10 | 30 min | M | Confirm date, location, and carrier contact. Remove personal items.
- **Pack "last out, first in" boxes + move-day kit** | M−9 | 2 hr | J | See the one-page checklist below.
- **Confirm Oregon internet install** | M−8 | 15 min | J | Confirm the appointment is still scheduled.

**Week 1 (M−7 to M−1)**
- **Confirm mover / truck and payment** | M−7 | 30 min | J | Confirm access, parking, and any permits.
- **Photograph valuables and serial numbers** | M−6 | 1 hr | J | Save to phone and a USB drive.
- **Defrost fridge and freezer** | M−5 | 30 min | J | Start 24 hours before loading.
- **Confirm dog overnight plans** | M−4 | 30 min | M | Confirm pet fees, food, and room access.
- **Confirm utility starts and shutoffs** | M−3 | 20 min | J | Confirm in writing.
- **Pack cleaning supplies and essentials** | M−2 | 2 hr | J | Keep the car kit separate.
- **Fill tank, check tires, pack car kit** | M−1 | 1 hr | M | See the one-page checklist.
- **Pack document folder into the car** | M−1 | 30 min | J | Originals stay with you.

**Move Day (M)**
- **MOVE DAY: walkthrough, keys, bill of lading** | M | Full day | J | Photo-document each room before leaving.

**Post-Move (+)**
- **Oregon vet visit** | M+1 | 1 hr | M | Transfer records and get the dog's new contact on file.

# Part 3: Moving-Day Essentials (Printable, One Page)

**Keep in the car, not on the truck.**

**DOCUMENTS (folder)**
☐ IDs and passports
☐ Vehicle titles and registrations
☐ Insurance cards and policy numbers
☐ Lease or closing papers
☐ Moving contract, inventory, Bill of Lading
☐ Mover / carrier phone numbers
☐ Dog records: rabies, vaccines, microchip #, meds, vet contact
☐ Prescriptions and medical contacts
☐ Cash, cards, and bank contact numbers

**DOG KIT**
☐ Food and water (for 2 days)
☐ Bowls, leash, harness, poop bags
☐ Meds and calming aids
☐ Blanket, familiar bed, favorite toy
☐ Crate or barrier

**CAR EMERGENCY KIT**
☐ Phone charger and car adapter
☐ Jumper cables or jump starter
☐ First-aid kit
☐ Water and snacks
☐ Flashlight, spare batteries
☐ Tire gauge and spare tire checked
☐ Tools: jack, lug wrench

**FIRST-NIGHT BOX (in your car)**
☐ Toiletries and towels
☐ Toilet paper
☐ Phone chargers and laptop
☐ One change of clothes each
☐ Coffee, mugs, and basic utensils
☐ Trash bags and paper towels
☐ Medications

**MOVE-DAY ROUTINE**
☐ Walkthrough photos (every room, closets, outside)
☐ Note meter readings
☐ Return keys, fobs, and remotes; get a receipt
☐ Sign Bill of Lading only after checking it
☐ Dog secured away from movers
☐ Mileage, fuel, and lodging receipts logged

**DRIVING DAYS**
☐ Start early; plan a break every 2–3 hours
☐ Walk the dog at each stop
☐ Never leave the dog alone in a parked car

## Recommendation: Quote B (National van line, binding-not-to-exceed)

**Why B wins on balance:**
- **Cost:** $3,400 is the lowest *guaranteed* price. A binding-not-to-exceed quote caps your total (barring changes in weight, service, or accessorials), so you can budget with confidence.
- **Risk:** The big risk is valuation. Standard coverage at $0.60/lb on ~6,200 lbs is roughly **$3,720 total**, which is a fraction of what your goods are worth. Budget $300–$500 to upgrade to Full Value Protection. That brings the realistic cost to about **$3,700–$3,900** and makes the risk manageable.
- **Convenience:** Portable storage (daily rental) lets you drop the move on a flexible schedule. A 9–12 day transit is slower, but you can plan around it with temporary housing.

**Why not the others:**
- **Quote A ($4,200):** Looks close to B, but "binding if weight OK" means the final price can rise if the weight comes in over 6,200 lbs. Full value protection is extra, and piano or appliance fees push it higher. Its 7–9 day transit is faster, though, so it's the strong runner-up if you need speed or have fragile or specialty items. Its real cost is likely $4,500–$5,000 with protection.
- **Quote C (~$1,900 + your time):** Cheapest by far, but you're driving 3 days, loading and unloading with hired labor, and you carry all the damage risk. Insurance through the rental company is limited. It also adds a car-driving burden, and your partner and dog share that time. Choose it only if money is the top constraint and you're comfortable with the logistics. Note that you'd still need car shipping or a second driver if both vehicles move.

**Decision rule:** If you need the goods within about a week of arrival and have fragile or specialty items, choose A. Otherwise, choose B with full value protection.

## Key Negotiation Points

**Quote A (local full-service)**
- Ask them to convert the "binding if weight OK" to a true binding-not-to-exceed.
- Get the piano/appliance surcharge in writing, with a fixed price if possible.
- Request full value protection included at no charge, or at least a quote for it.
- Ask them to reduce the $500 deposit or accept payment on delivery.

**Quote B (national van line)**
- Lock in the $3,400 as binding-not-to-exceed, and confirm which accessorials (fuel, stairs, shuttle) are excluded.
- Negotiate the full value protection price into the base quote.
- Ask for the $300 deposit to be credited toward the final bill.
- Ask for free or reduced portable storage days, and a firm delivery window.

**Quote C (DIY)**
- Ask the rental company to include the truck insurance upgrade in the rate.
- Negotiate labor rates or a flat fee for the full day.
- Book the truck early for a lower one-way rate, and confirm mileage limits and fuel policy.

## 6 Must-Ask Questions

**Quote A (local full-service)**
1. What is the exact price if the final weight is over 6,200 lbs?
2. Is the estimate binding, and under what conditions can it change?
3. What's the full value protection cost per $1,000 declared, and what's the deductible?
4. What are the piano, appliance, and stair surcharges, and are they capped?
5. Will you do a physical or video survey before final pricing?
6. Who is the carrier of record, and what is the USDOT number and cargo insurance amount?

**Quote B (national van line)**

4. What is the daily rate for portable storage, and how many free days are included?
5. Is this a brokered move, and who is the actual carrier and what is their USDOT number?
6. What is the earliest pickup and delivery window, and what happens if the carrier misses it?

**Quote C (DIY)**
1. What insurance options does the rental company offer, and what do they cover and exclude?
2. What are the mileage limits, fuel policy, and one-way drop fees?
3. Are the two movers insured, and do they carry their own liability coverage?
4. What is the cancellation policy for the labor booking, and is there a minimum hour charge?
5. What's the total cost if the drive takes an extra day or the truck breaks down?
6. Can the truck be dropped off in Oregon, and are there any Ohio or Oregon restrictions on the rental?

turns.task: plan the driving route with the dog

turns.content:
Yes. Before I lay out a route, I need a few details. Here's what I'm assuming, so you can correct anything:

**Assumptions (from our budget)**
- **Start:** Columbus, OH. **End:** Portland, OR. Distance is about 2,400 to 2,500 miles.
- **Move Day:** Friday 01/15/2027. You're driving the car (Scenario A), with the dog.
- **Budget:** 2 pet-friendly nights of lodging, and about 4 days of meals and fuel.
- **Driving pace:** about 8 hours of driving per day, with breaks every 2 to 3 hours.

**Questions to finalize the plan**
1. **Driving days:** Is 4 days (about 600 miles per day) OK, or would you prefer 5 days with lighter driving? Winter weather on I-80 and I-84 can add time.
2. **Route preference:** Do you want the fastest interstate route (I-70/I-80 across Nebraska, Wyoming, and Idaho, then I-84 into Oregon), or a southern route (I-70 to I-40 or I-15)? The northern route is more exposed to January snow. The southern route avoids most mountain passes but is longer.
3. **Dog details:** How old is the dog, and does it do well in the car for long stretches? Any medications, anxiety, or motion sickness?
4. **Lodging:** Do you want a set list of pet-friendly hotels, or should I suggest criteria (for example, ground-floor rooms, pet fee caps, and cancellation policies) so you can book?
5. **Departure:** Is a dawn start (around 6 a.m. Eastern) acceptable so you arrive before dark?

**Winter safety items to plan for**
- Check I-80 (Wyoming and Nebraska) and I-84 (Oregon Blue Mountains) road conditions the morning you leave and each morning after.
- Carry chains or check your tire condition, and keep a winter kit (blanket, water, food, shovel) in the car.
- Keep the dog's water and food accessible, and plan walk stops at rest areas with plowed space.

Once you answer those questions, I'll give you a day-by-day itinerary with mileage, stop times, pet-friendly stops, and a backup plan for weather closures.

turns.task: plan the driving route with the dog

turns.content:
Yes. I'll sketch a route now, and you can answer the questions at the end to refine it.

**Correction to my last message:** I-80 doesn't cross Idaho. The northern route runs I-70 west to Indianapolis, then I-74/I-80 west through Illinois and Iowa, I-80 across Nebraska and Wyoming to Salt Lake City, then I-84 through Idaho and Oregon. This route is about 2,500 to 2,700 miles, longer than the 2,400 to 2,500 I assumed. Check the exact figure in a routing app.

**Two budget issues to fix first**
- **Nights:** Four driving days need three overnight stops. Your budget covers two nights. Five driving days need four nights, so add about $300 to $600 for lodging.
- **Daily pace:** At about 2,600 miles, four days means roughly 650 miles per day, which is hard in January. Five days (about 520 per day) is more realistic with a dog. Six days (about 430 per day) is the most comfortable and includes a weather buffer.

**Sample 5-day skeleton (approximate; verify in a routing app)**

| Day | Route | Approx. miles | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Columbus to central Illinois (Bloomington/Peoria area) | ~430 | Shorter first day to test the dog's car tolerance |
| 2 | Central Illinois to Omaha, NE (via Des Moines) | ~500 | Check I-80 Iowa conditions |
| 3 | Omaha to Laramie or Cheyenne, WY | ~500 | Highest winter risk. Leave early and check I-80 closures |
| 4 | Cheyenne to Salt Lake City, UT | ~530 | Longest day. Be ready to stop at Rock Springs or Evanston if I-80 closes |
| 5 | Salt Lake City to Boise, ID, then Portland | ~340 + ~430 | Shorten if needed by ending in Boise and finishing the next morning |

**Dog-specific planning**
- Stop every 2 to 3 hours for a 10 to 15 minute walk. Use rest areas with plowed space.
- Keep water and food in the cabin, not the cargo area. Feed lightly 2 hours before driving.
- Never leave the dog in the car unattended, even briefly, at fuel stops. Temperatures can drop below freezing.
- Book pet-friendly hotels with ground-floor rooms and cancellation policies before you leave.
- Do a practice drive of at least 2 hours before the trip to test motion sickness and anxiety.

**Winter safety**
- Check I-80 (Wyoming and Utah) and I-84 (Blue Mountains, Oregon) road conditions each morning. Use the state DOT apps and 511 services.
- Carry chains or confirm all-weather or winter tires, and keep a winter kit: blanket, water, food, shovel, flashlight, and a dog blanket.
- Keep at least half a tank of fuel at all times, and plan fuel stops before mountain passes.

**To finalize the itinerary, please tell me:**
1. Do you want 5 days (four nights) or 6 days for the dog's comfort?
2. How old is the dog, and how does it handle long car rides, anxiety, or motion sickness? Any medications?
3. Are you planning to leave early in the morning, around 6 a.m. Eastern?
4. Do you want a list of pet-friendly hotel criteria, or specific hotel options along each leg?

Once you answer, I'll build a day-by-day itinerary with stop times, pet-friendly stops, and a backup plan for weather closures.
